PZMH20PerformativePrediction.measureWass.reason: Compared Theorem 3.8 at cited publication:373-415 under the bound corrected target for theorem-3.8-general-measure-analytic-bridge with the full expanded target, roles 1-35, and every listed support display. The model and analytic premises quantify expected-loss/gradient integrability, local loss measurability, actual pointwise gradients, two-coordinate beta-gradient Lipschitz bounds, gamma-strong convexity, and epsilon-Wasserstein sensitivity over all ambient parameters and the chosen data carrier, as the corrected scope expressly requires. The coupling expansion uses prescribed probability marginals and the infimum of finite integrable expected-distance costs. The domain is nonempty, closed and convex; the projection lands in it, satisfies the stated variational inequality, and is nonexpansive. The update expands to projection of theta minus eta times the loss gradient averaged under D(theta). The numerical assumptions are exactly 0 < gamma <= beta, 0 < eta <= 2/(gamma+beta), and epsilon < gamma/((gamma+beta)(1+3 eta beta/2)). Both the pairwise bound and iterate bound use q = 1 - eta*(gamma beta/(gamma+beta) - epsilon*(3 eta beta^2/2+beta)). These premises give 0 <= q < 1, and the q^t bound implies the displayed logarithmic convergence-time guarantee. The conclusion includes existence and uniqueness among all domain-stable points and convergence from each domain initial point. The ambient analytic scope is accepted only as the disclosed non-equivalent corrected target.

The concluding claim role is exactly the source distance bound, with no dropped conclusion or additional optimal/stable uniqueness premise. No corrected-target record is invoked.

Compared the selected proposition_3_6_counterexamples_c source item, its identity-bound approved correction for proposition-3.6c-arbitrary-regularity-constants, the complete expanded Spec and claim roles, and all 17 displayed prerequisites. PMLR PDF page 5 visibly states epsilon >= gamma/beta; the extracted text loses the non-strict glyph and fraction layout. The approved correction expressly adds gamma <= beta and disclaims archival equivalence. For every positive epsilon, beta, gamma satisfying these two inequalities, the displayed real-valued model has D(theta) = delta_(1 + epsilon*theta), loss gamma*x^2/2 - beta*z*x, and actual gradient gamma*x - beta*z. Its parameter-gradient and data-gradient Lipschitz constants are respectively gamma <= beta and beta, and its gamma-strong-convexity inequality holds with the required gamma/2 remainder. Dirac laws make every frozen loss integrable and give W1 = epsilon*|theta-theta_prime| through the displayed finite-cost coupling definition. Frozen risk is minimized over all real candidates by G(theta) = (beta/gamma)*(1 + epsilon*theta), exactly the expanded RRM predicate. Writing G(theta) = a*theta + b gives a = epsilon*beta/gamma >= 1 and b = beta/gamma > 0; from initial 0, the iterates are at least n*b and tend to +infinity. Equality epsilon = gamma/beta is therefore covered by positive translation. The complete quantified claim matches the approved corrected target, with no additional restriction on its admissible constants and no archival-equivalence claim.

The displayed finite-law, expectation, metric, coupling, and sensitivity definitions give these clauses their stated meanings, so the witness establishes the source conclusion.
